## MIP Display Impact on Battery Life
Building on battery findings from prior research, MIP displays used by Garmin and COROS have been found to be power-efficient, drawing power only when pixels change. This is because every pixel has its own small memory cell and the pixel is only refreshed if a value changes. As a result, MIP displays are much more efficient on battery life, especially when compared to AMOLED displays. In fact, MIP watches like the FR955 don't need to turn the display off, unlike AMOLED watches like the FR965, as the screen only dims but doesn't turn off after a set timeout value.

The power efficiency of MIP displays is particularly noticeable in bright outdoor conditions, where they can remain visible without consuming significant battery power. In contrast, LCD and AMOLED displays need to shine brighter than the sun, resulting in higher battery consumption. However, it's worth noting that MIP displays may not be as bright as AMOLED displays, which can be a drawback in certain situations.

## MIP vs. OLED/AMOLED/LCD: Power Consumption and Visuals

MIP (Memory-in-Pixel) displays, prominently featured in smartwatches from brands like Garmin and COROS, demonstrate significant power efficiency advantages, particularly for always-on functionality. Building on prior findings, MIP displays are inherently power-efficient because each pixel contains its own small memory cell, drawing power only when that pixel's value changes. This unique architecture allows MIP watches to keep their screens constantly on without incurring significant battery drain, directly addressing the growing demand for longer battery life in smartwatches.

In contrast, OLED and AMOLED displays, while known for their vibrant colors and deep blacks, require a continuous power source for their light-emitting pixels to function. This fundamental difference means that maintaining an always-on display with OLED technology typically consumes more power than with MIP. Even with advancements like lower refresh rates, the energy lost through LTPS leakage can counteract potential power savings if pixels are not truly static, as constant updates demand more energy.

## Real-World Battery Life: MIP vs OLED Always-On Display Technology

Smartwatch battery life has become a critical differentiator in the wearables market, with display technology emerging as the primary factor influencing endurance. When comparing MIP (Memory-in-Pixel) displaysused by brands like Garmin and COROS against the OLED panels found in Apple and Samsung watches, the architectural differences in how each technology powers its pixels create fundamentally different user experiences—especially when always-on display (AOD) is enabled.

**The MIP Advantage**

MIP displays achieve their exceptional power efficiency through a unique pixel memory architecture. Each individual pixel contains its own dedicated memory cell, allowing the screen to maintain an image without continuous power application. Unlike traditional displays that require constant refresh signals, MIP panels only consume meaningful power when a pixel's value actually changes. This means a watch face displaying the same time and complications for hours draws minimal current—essentially just enough to maintain the static image state.
